learningObjectives: Identify TypeScript types and interfaces used in frontend applications.
Add type safety to component props and application data.
Use TypeScript to detect common JavaScript development errors.

activities.title: TypeScript Type Explorer
activities.instruction: Click each type to explore the kind of value it can represent.

content.concept: TypeScript provides static types such as string, number, boolean, arrays, objects, and unions to describe the values used by an application.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

descriptions: Represents a collection of values, often with a defined element type.
Represents structured data with named properties.
Allows a value to be one of several specified types.

activities.title: Interface Anatomy
activities.instruction: Explore the parts of a TypeScript interface.

content.concept: An interface describes the expected shape of an object by defining its property names and types.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

descriptions: Defines a required name property containing a string.
Defines a required age property containing a number.
Defines an optional email property containing a string.

activities.title: Type Error Detector
activities.instruction: Choose the example that contains a TypeScript type mismatch.

content.concept: Static type checking can detect incompatible assignments and function arguments during development before the code is executed.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

activities.title: Typed Component Builder
activities.instruction: Build the structure of a React component with typed props.

content.concept: TypeScript can define the shape of React component props so incorrect or missing values can be detected during development.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.
